Title: Boulder City Council Regular Meeting - September 21, 2023
Overview: At its September 21, 2023 regular meeting, the Boulder City Council presented Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day declarations, heard public comment on topics including a library building, a Central Park homeless camping incident, and local housing, and approved its consent agenda. The council also unanimously approved Boulder Junction Phase 2 Transit Village Area Plan amendments and approved the affordable and modest-size housing zoning ordinance on second reading with changes, deferring several proposed amendments to a later phase. Council agreed to send a letter to the County Commissioners supporting a proposed affordable housing tax ballot measure and requesting support for permanent supportive housing.

Topic1.Title: Hispanic Heritage Month and Energy Efficiency Day Declarations
Topic1.Summary: Council presented a Hispanic Heritage Month declaration, with Spanish interpretation and remarks from community interpreters and advocates on language justice. Council then presented an Energy Efficiency Day declaration, highlighting energy efficiency's economic and climate benefits and designating October 2023 as Energy Efficiency Day.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic2.Summary: Eight in-person speakers and one virtual speaker addressed council on topics including a library building disposition, a Black history museum exhibit, a homeless camping incident near Central Park, a child-friendly restroom request, a police incident at a hardware store, historic house demolition review, and the 28th and J middle-income housing project. Staff responded on the Central Park incident and child-friendly cities initiative, and council members commented on the library buildings and public safety.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda and Call-Up Check-In
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3F unanimously by roll call vote. For the call-up check-in on a Life Sciences facility at Walnut Street, a council member expressed interest in calling it up for its sustainability leadership, but no member called it up.

Topic4.Title: Boulder Junction Phase 2 Transit Village Area Plan Amendments
Topic4.Summary: Staff presented amendments to the Transit Village Area Plan phase two covering land use categories (mutod, mui, pkuo), urban design, and transportation connections, along with a chapter five summary update. Staff noted market analysis favoring residential uses and the need for business stabilization strategies. Planning board recommended approval with a revision removing office from the neighborhood Tod place type, which staff did not support. Council approved both motions unanimously by roll call vote.

Topic5.Title: Affordable and Modest Size Housing Zoning Ordinance 8599
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented an ordinance amending land use code provisions on site review, density, parking, and subdivision standards to encourage affordable, middle, and modest-sized housing. Changes included exempting certain middle housing from site review, replacing unit-based density with floor area ratios, reducing parking requirements, and allowing duplexes and triplexes in some low-density zones. Council discussed numerous amendments, deferred several to a future phase two, and approved the ordinance on second reading with changes unanimously, with third reading to follow on consent.

Topic6.Title: Letter Supporting County Affordable Housing Ballot Measure
Topic6.Summary: Council member Benjamin proposed a letter to County Commissioners endorsing a proposed affordable and attainable housing tax ballot measure and requesting support for permanent supportive housing with substantial wraparound services and transitional housing. Council agreed to send the letter, with formal endorsement to be considered later through a hotline request.
